title: A maximal bad quotient for Popescu approximation
statement: Let $R\to\Lambda$ be a regular ring map [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] for which $\Lambda$ is not a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-smooth-algebras]. There exist Noetherian rings $R\prime,\Lambda\prime$ and a regular map $R\prime\to\Lambda\prime$, with $R\prime\ne0$, such that $\Lambda\prime$ is not a filtered colimit of smooth $R\prime$-algebras, but for every nonzero ideal $J\subset R\prime$, $\Lambda\prime/J\Lambda\prime$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $R\prime/J$-algebras. The source ring remains in the universe of $R$, and the target remains in the universe of $\Lambda$.

proof.text: Consider the set of ideals I that are zero or whose induced quotient map is bad. It is nonempty without using quotient-zero transport. Apply set_has_maximal_iff_noetherian to select a maximal I. If its membership is supplied by I=0, keep the original R and Λ; maximality directly gives ind-smoothness modulo every nonzero ideal. Otherwise its quotient map is bad, and construct R/I and Λ/IΛ. Both quotient rings are Noetherian by Mathlib instances.

The quotient map is regular: regular_base_change applies along R→R/I. Identify the resulting tensor product with Λ/IΛ using quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor and commRight. A proved private helper transports flatness and geometric regularity through the resulting algebra equivalence.

A proved private helper shows any bad algebra has nontrivial base: a subsingleton base forces a subsingleton target, which is smooth by the zero-algebra standard-smooth instances. ObjectProperty.le_ind contradicts badness. Apply this helper to the original map in the zero branch and to the quotient map in the bad-quotient branch.

For a nonzero ideal J of R/I, K=J.comap(Quotient.mk I) strictly contains I: the kernel gives containment; equality would yield J=0 after mapping back along the surjection. Maximality implies ind-smoothness modulo K. Apply Algebra.ind_smooth_quotient_compatibility with I≤K, then rewrite map(comap J)=J by quotient-map surjectivity to get the required ind-smoothness modulo J. Assemble these data as the required witnesses.

proof_origin.note: Maximality with a separate zero branch, regularity from base change and algebra equivalence, and existing ind-smooth quotient compatibility.

theorem exists_popescu_maximal_bad_quotient
    (R : Type u) (Λ : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra R Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing Λ]
    (hreg : RingHom.IsRegular (algebraMap R Λ))
    (hbad : ¬ ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
      (fun B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} R ↦ Algebra.Smooth R B) (CommAlgCat.of R Λ)) :
    ∃ (R' : Type u) (Λ' : Type (max u v)) (_ : CommRing R') (_ : CommRing Λ')
      (_ : Algebra R' Λ') (_ : IsNoetherianRing R') (_ : IsNoetherianRing Λ')
      (_ : Nontrivial R'),
      RingHom.IsRegular (algebraMap R' Λ') ∧
      (¬ ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
        (fun B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} R' ↦ Algebra.Smooth R' B) (CommAlgCat.of R' Λ')) ∧
      ∀ (I : Ideal R'), I ≠ ⊥ →
        ObjectProperty.ind.{max u v}
          (fun B : CommAlgCat.{max u v} (R' ⧸ I) ↦ Algebra.Smooth (R' ⧸ I) B)
          (CommAlgCat.of (R' ⧸ I) (Λ' ⧸ I.map (algebraMap R' Λ')))
